records.question: What does a production AI agent stack need beyond the model's own reasoning and tool-use loop?
records.title: Beyond the model loop: four responsibilities a production agent stack must separate
records.one_liner: ReAct, OPA, Temporal and the enterprise-agent production model describe different responsibilities; together they form a useful layered mental model, but none of the sources claims this exact combined stack.
records.thesis: A model can reason and select actions without supplying production authority, durable orchestration, reconstructable execution evidence or application-specific outcome verification. Treat those as separate responsibilities that may be composed, not as features of one universal agent framework.

consensus.statement: Choosing an action is not the same responsibility as authorizing, safely executing and later verifying a consequential action.
Durable, reconstructable execution state is a production concern separate from the transient process that happens to perform one step.

layers.name: Reason / act / observe
layers.does: Interleave reasoning, environment actions and returned observations so new evidence can change the next decision.
layers.does_not: Provide production authorization, durable workflow state or guaranteed business-side-effect safety.

layers.name: Policy decision
layers.does: Compute a policy decision from explicit input, policy and data while keeping the protected application as the enforcement point.
layers.does_not: Perform, durably record or verify the protected business action itself.

layers.name: Durable orchestration
layers.does: Persist workflow progress outside any one Worker and coordinate retryable work through durable execution history.
layers.does_not: Turn external side effects into exactly-once outcomes automatically.

layers.name: Controlled execution substrate
layers.does: Frame authority, protected-data boundaries, intervention and reconstructable execution evidence around consequential agent work.
layers.does_not: Specify one mandatory policy engine, workflow runtime or model reasoning method.

reviewed_disagreements.why_it_matters: ReAct and controlled execution discuss agent actions at different layers; treating them as competing architectures creates a false contradiction.
OPA narrows one control responsibility inside the broader production model; it does not replace the execution substrate.

unresolved_gaps.statement: None of the sources establishes that ReAct + OPA + Temporal + one controlled-execution layer is a canonical or universally appropriate implementation stack.
Application-specific outcome verification remains a separate design problem: permission, orchestration and execution history do not by themselves prove that the intended business result is correct.

visual_plan.title: Separate responsibilities before choosing tools
visual_plan.caption: The four layers are a project synthesis across sources. They are not a source-authored reference architecture.
